pages.api:
# API reference

> The readings, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Reading `event/<name>` (default `can-anomaly0`)

`event.v1`, class `reading`: `kind` (`can.baseline`, `can.new_id`, `can.dlc_change`, `can.id_missing`, `can.id_back`, `can.rate_high`, `can.rate_low`, `can.flood`), `severity` (`info`, `warn`, `alert`), `subject` (`0x1a4`, `0x18ff0001` for an extended id, `bus`), `detail`, and `value` when there is a number (a rate, a length code, the id count).

## Reading `telemetry/<name>`

`telemetry.v1`: `frames.seen`, `baseline.ids`, `events`, `monitoring`, `records.skipped`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout

One JSON line per event, then one report per interval:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `phase` | string | `learning` or `monitoring` |
| `frames_seen`, `baseline_ids`, `baseline_frames_per_s` | numbers | |
| `events`, `events_by_kind` | number, object | not counting the baseline event |
| `last_events` | array | the five latest |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `subscribed`, `published`, `skipped_records`, `error` |

## Store vector (id 39)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | `frames_seen` |
| 1 | `baseline_ids` |
| 2 | `events` |
| 3 | `new_ids` |
| 4 | `missing_ids` |
| 5 | `rate_events` (high plus low) |
| 6 | `floods` |
| 7 | `monitoring` (0 learning, 1 watching) |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8073`, continuous mode)

`/status`, `/raw`, `/history`, `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--source`, `--name`, `--learn-s`, `--window-s`, `--rate-high-x`, `--rate-low-frac`, `--cooldown-s`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.baseline:
# The baseline

> What is learned, what is compared, and what each event means.

## Learning

For **Learning time** after start, per id (a standard 11-bit id and an extended 29-bit id with the same number are different ids) the cog counts frames and notes the data lengths used. It publishes one `can.baseline` event when it finishes, saying how many ids and frames per second it learned.

## Watching

In windows of **Check window** (5 s), against the baseline:

| Event | Severity | When |
|---|---|---|
| `can.new_id` | warn | an id that was not learned sends, once per id |
| `can.dlc_change` | info | a known id uses a data length it never used, once per length |
| `can.id_missing` | warn | an id that sent 0.5 frames/s or more is silent for two windows or five of its periods, whichever is longer |
| `can.id_back` | info | that id sends again |
| `can.rate_high` | warn | an id runs above 3 times its baseline and 5 frames/s over it |
| `can.rate_low` | warn | an id of 2 frames/s or more runs under a quarter of its baseline but still sends |
| `can.flood` | alert | the whole bus runs above 3 times its baseline total and 50 frames/s over it |

A rate event for the same id does not repeat within **Repeat time** (30 s).

## Time

The clock is the frames' own timestamps, so a recorded log replays exactly as the bus did. On a quiet live bus the cog advances its clock from the wall clock, so silence is noticed.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-can-anomaly --once --simulate                       # synthetic bus, virtual time
cog-can-anomaly --once --replay drive.log --learn-s 20  # a candump -L log
cog-can-anomaly --source can0                           # live, from the broker
```

Each event is printed as a JSON line and, when watching live, published. Replay and simulation only print.

## Placed on a node

Place `can-anomaly` in the same project as `can-fd`. Its `cog.toml` declares the input `can.frame` and the outputs `event` and `telemetry`. It declares no device.

## Choosing when to start

Start it with the bus in its normal state. Restarting it relearns, so a restart also clears a baseline that learned something abnormal.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Hear about a bus that changed without watching it.

`can-anomaly` reads the frames `can-fd` publishes. For its first 30 seconds it only learns which ids send and how fast. After that it tells you, as `event.v1` readings on `event/can-anomaly0`, when an id appears that was not there, a periodic id goes quiet, an id runs much faster or slower, or the bus is flooded.

## The short path

1. **Run `can-fd`** on the bus. → see its guide
2. **Start this cog while the bus is doing what is normal.** Whatever it sees in the first 30 seconds is the baseline. → see **The baseline**
3. **Try it without a bus.** `cog-can-anomaly --once --simulate` runs a synthetic bus with a new id, a silent id and a burst through the engine and prints the events.
4. **Place it** with `can-fd`. → see **Set up**

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- **Counts, not meaning.** It knows ids and rates, not what a message says. It does not read the data bytes, so a changed value in a known id passes unseen. Rates, ids and silence catch a node that was added, removed, stuck or babbling.
- **A baseline is what it saw.** A bus that was already faulty while learning is learned as normal; an id that sends only on events (a door, a diagnostic reply) may be silent while learning and then looks new when it speaks.
- **Slow ids are not judged for silence.** Only ids that sent at least 0.5 frames/s while learning can go missing; below 2 frames/s there is no low-rate event.
- **No decisions.** It reports; whoever reads the events decides.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

`no broker: WEFTOS_COGBUS is not set` from a shell without a broker; otherwise `bus.error` has the broker's refusal (`unauthorized` or `unknown_topic`: placed without its `[[inputs]]`; `cross_project`: `can-fd` is in another project).

## `phase` stays `learning`

The learning time runs on the frames' clock. With no frames arriving the cog advances from the wall clock, so it ends after **Learning time** regardless; if `frames_seen` is zero then, the baseline is empty and every id will look new. Check that `can-fd` is publishing.

## Too many `can.new_id` events

The bus has event-driven ids that were quiet while learning. Learn longer, or start the cog while the bus is busy.

## `skipped_records` grows

The cog fell behind the stream (a very busy bus). Frames are skipped, rates are understated and `rate_low` may fire; reduce the other load on the node.

## No events at all although the bus changed

The change is in data values, not ids, lengths or rates. This cog does not read data bytes.

# Sensor guide for can-anomaly (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md).

schema = 1
title = "Spotting what is new on a CAN bus"
sensor = "The can.frame stream of the can-fd cog"
cog = "can-anomaly"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "baseline", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
baseline = "baseline"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "can.frame/can0"
detail = "every data frame"

[[flow]]
name = "can-anomaly cog"
detail = "learn ids and rates, then compare"

[[flow]]
name = "event/can-anomaly0"
detail = "event.v1"
